ES-3 May Be Compact and Lightweight but Built Like Serious Campers – Can House up to Five People
14 photos
Photo: RS-Camp
Hopping into your truck or 4x4 on the weekend and heading out to the middle of nowhere to catch a sky full of stars is how some people center and ground their souls, and generally, there are two ways to do so: either with an overly-equipped RV or motorhome or a bare-minimum travel trailer with the smallest profile possible. Today, we’ll be diving deeper into a habitat of the latter category.
It’s called the ES-3, and is officially the most compact solution from RS-Camp, a German team that’s been on the market for a few years now but who have somehow eluded our seeking eyes. What makes this unit so special and what we can do with one is the very purpose of this short article.
Photo: RS-Camp As mentioned, this is the smallest unit from RS-Camp, and as such, you’d expect it to only be suitable for up to two guests, maybe three. Well, RS-Camp is a bit different than other teams and what we have before us can actually be equipped to handle the lifestyle of up to five guests.
This is made possible with an expandable design which, while it may be light weight and compact, can still be decked out to the teeth with all we need for those five guests. This includes the essential roof-top tent, outdoor bathroom annex with shower, some light off-grid power solutions, and most importantly, the ability to drive deep into the unknown. Let’s start with the latter.
At it’s core, the ES-3 is built upon a trailing A-arm suspension, a tested and proven setup, one that not only means a plush ride while you’re out and about, but also has the effect of prolonging your camper’s lifespan by reducing the amount of vibrations the shell is exposed to, not to mention extreme torsional forces.
Photo: RS-Camp As for the lightweight side of the story, the ES-3 rolls in with a dry weight of just 520 kg (1,146 lbs) and is said to have a GVWR of 750 kg (1,653 lbs), a limit in Europe that allows drivers to operate it with a standard B Class license (D Class for USA).
This low weight is achieved with the use of one of my favorite building blocks that the RV and camper industry has been calling upon for decades: fiberglass. With this composite goodness, RS gives rise to a camper that’s seamless and edgeless and protected from the elements with a layer of bed liner on top.
If you’re aware of the use of bed liner over a campers exterior, you know that it’s a pretty darned good way to really keep water and the elements from eating away at your shell, but you also know that it’s protected against hits and eventual stones kicked up into it. It’s not bulletproof, but it is a great way to protect your unit, and an inexpensive one at that.
Photo: RS-Camp Lining your camper’s exterior can even be done with some cans of the stuff; I’ve covered DIY projects where builders called upon a box of bed liner cans to seal the exterior of a garage-built teardrop camper or other smaller RVs.
As for the inexpensive side of the story, a standard ES-3 is priced at no more than €16,900, which is roughly $18,500 (at current exchange rates), so it’s not the cheapest composite camper you can find on the market, but it is one that will be in your family for longer than most cookie-cutter options the market offers, especially in the US.
Now, a compact camper means limited space and this is true for the ES-3 as well, but it doesn’t have to mean that you can stuff it full of goodies and features we call upon while under the stars; you just need to pack it up properly is all.
Photo: RS-Camp To do so, RS-Camp called upon a trick that the camper and RV industry has been utilizing for years: moving the kitchen to the rear of the RV . It’s a trait that we first saw in teardrop campers of old and is still as applicable today as ever.
But, RS also integrated a storage option at the front of the camper, in the shape of a utility box and that roof-rail system on top, the latter standing as the best place for all your goodies, at least, the ones that can be exposed to the elements while traveling. Don’t forget that you can also toss items into your box with wheels while traveling.
Keep in mind that most features in the kitchen and the off-grid power system are extra, annex and awnings too, so have some extra bucks ready to go for this one. As an idea of how much, you can either bring your own gear and shop for the best deals around, or go through RS.
Photo: RS-Camp Just keep in mind that a shower tent from RS is €500, a 43-liter fridge will run you €850, and a lithium battery with 100 Ah is close to €1,000. The reason for the premium on these items would be their integration into your unit and the fact that they are meant to work perfectly with the ES-3. Look into a braking setup and anti-sway if you want to load up the unit with more than its weight limit.
The last place we haven’t looked is inside this camper, a space that is ready for two adults and possibly one child, and some of their belongings, although, limited to what we can stuff into the two cabinets at the foot of the mattress; the rest goes outside.
While picking up an ES-3 is rather simple and easy for Europeans, for Americans to get their hands on this camper we need roughly $3,500 for shipping and around another $1,000 or so for import feess, port handling, and other paperwork.
Is it better to shop locally? Well, there are some teams in the US that can offer a similar product, and for a similar price too. Have a look at the coverage we’ve run on campers to find some of them. Until next time.

Juiced Bikes Gives Our Little Ones a Chance To Join Us on Rides – Drops Scrambler Mini E-Bike
12 photos
Photo: Juiced Bikes
Let’s face it: most e-bikes are destined for adults, especially since some can catch speeds well over any legal speed limits, leaving children on the sidelines or begging their parents to “hand them the keys,” so to speak. This, however, creates a bit of a niche, one that some brands are starting to tap into.
One crew that’s doing just that seems to be none other than Juiced Bikes, the one and the same that’s been around since 2009 and which now supplies countless cities across the US, and usually, in the scrambler styling that several brands on the market are calling upon.
Photo: Juiced Bikes While Juiced has been focused on bringing larger bikes to the market, those aimed at adult and young adult use, the latest, the Scrambler Mini, rolls in with a smaller frame, has slightly less powerful components, granting us a top speed of just 20 mph (32 kph), and a lower weight. Did I mention price tag? All these traits place it on the menu for younger riders, be they slightly pre-teen, or young teenagers.
In terms of sizes and ages, Juiced’s website mentions that riders as tall as 4 ft have a place on the Mini and those over 5 ft 3 in, should look somewhere else. It also weighs 59 lbs (27 kg), so it is a bit heavy for a kid, to say the least, but it should help them understand and learn the mechanics of riding such an e-bike. In a few years down the line, you may end up buying them a dirt bike anyway.
Aside from a smaller frame and a dumbed down 500 W (nominal motor), Juiced also ensures that riders are as safe as possible, and to do that, wheel size is also reduced to 16 inches, bringing the whole frame lower to the ground and boosting the center of gravity. It also makes for easier mounting and dismounting, essential for smaller riders.
Photo: Juiced Bikes More on the side of comfort and safety , Juiced did add a front fork to the Mini, and while it doesn’t boast the most amount of travel on the market, the 50 mm our kids can access will help in reducing some of the bumps the front wheel takes and helping stay in control on rougher ground. The fat tires will also assist in reducing vibrations while riding.
The tires added to the bike also carry a four-inch cross-section, and this means extra traction, allowing our young ones to follow us through a wide range of terrains and riding seasons. The larger contact patch also means that braking should be more effective, which is also aided by a pair of hydraulic disc brakes with 180 mm rotors. That’s ample stopping power, even for someone my size.
Since bikes of this nature often make it difficult to pedal, at least, comfortably, thumb throttle is also added to the Mini, and it allows kids to learn how to use this function, again, preparing them for larger and faster machines down the line. But, it’s also essential since the Mini is only rocking a single-speed drivetrain, and in a city with hills, it would be extremely difficult to get moving.
Photo: Juiced Bikes What does help in tackling hills and ensuring your kid stands a chance in keeping up with you when riding around on the outskirts of town is the 80 Nm (59 lb-ft) of torque the motor can spit out. Four speed settings allow our little ones to stay in control and speed can be limited by a menu accessed through a personalized pin.
Speaking of riding around, I do need to point out that the max range for the Mini stands at just 40 miles (64 km), and this is a number that’s sure to drop if you choose to tackle tougher terrain, have a larger rider, and even how much throttle you use.
All this brings me to where we started this whole Scrambler Mini goodness: What it allows us to tap into. Aside from being the obvious, an e-bike that grants our kids access to electrification, it’s also a great way to bond with your kid, placing you both side-by-side while out and about, and that right there is the real benefit of making a bringing an electric bicycle destined for kids to the market.
Photo: Juiced Bikes Juiced clearly has a benefit in all this too, making it possible to pair your kid’s e-bike with one for you, and one that even looks like their own. Heck, once they outgrow the Mini , just pass them your own steed that you’ve been riding for the past couple of years and get yourself something new, or do it the other way around: get them a new ride. For Juiced, this means more business, and a smart way to scoop up some cash that other brands are missing.
All this brings us to the price of a Mini. Currently, Juiced is selling this one for $850 (€775), so quite the acceptable price, if you ask me. Be sure to teach your child responsible riding and the importance of at least rocking a helmet.

Hyundai Motor Launches the All-New, Eighth-Generation i30 Sedan in Australia - Yes, It's the Elantra
14 photos
Photo: Hyundai
The South Korean automaker should really decide on a single moniker for its long-running series of compact cars, which has been around since 1990 and has now reached its eighth generation.
Of course, we are talking about the Hyundai Elantra series – but South Korean fans or Australian enthusiasts might raise an eyebrow. That’s because they know it as the Hyundai Avante at home in Korea or the i30 Sedan Down Under.
Over the years, the Hyundai Elantra was also dubbed the Hyundai Lantra, Bimantara Nenggala, i35 Elantra, and gained the i30 Sedan moniker starting with the seventh generation back in 2020 for Australia. Anyway, the eighth-generation Elantra’s first introduction came as the Avante at home in South Korea back in June during the Busan International Mobility Show.
Now, though, the Australian market has synchronized with the global model as the all-new Elantra premiered in North America at the 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show in both ICE and hybrid formats. However, the all-new i30 Sedan, Hyundai Motor's eighth-generation compact sedan, is coming to the Land Down Under starting in the first half of next year, with the hybrid powertrain only.
Hyundai Motor says it has “redefined” the small sedan with the all-new i30 Sedan, mixing “segment-leading style and space, hybrid performance enhanced by ‘intelligent efficiency’ and Pleos Connect's software experience.” The car adopts Hyundai Motor's 'Art of Steel' design language that’s also present on the new Tucson and brings to life H-Edge lighting, increased dimensions, and “furniture-inspired comfort,” whatever that may mean, all the while also “maintaining the agility and efficiency of a small sedan.”
Hyundai says the new i30 Sedan has medium-sized car interior space along with enhanced hybrid performance thanks to the Intelligent Hybrid System, which includes predictive energy management and the Smart Regeneration System 3.0. Of course, there are also new colors: Kodiak Blue Pearl, Kodiak Blue Matte, Raptor Gray Matte, and Graphene Green Pearl – the signature hue.
Inside, the company has introduced a 12.9-inch Pleos Connect display, a slim information display, dual wireless charging (Qi 2.0 – 15W), audio by Bang & Olufsen, Hyundai Digital Key 2, and 100W ultra-fast charging USB ports, along with six color combinations: Black/Black, Black/Dove Grey, Black/Cognac, Burgundy/Rose Ivory, Black/Chalk Beige, and Chalk Beige.
The 2027 Hyundai i30 Sedan has two powertrains in Australia : 1.6-liter hybrid and a regular 2.0-liter gasoline. The electrified option has 115 kW or 157 ps (154 hp) and a six-speed dual-clutch transmission plus Smart Regeneration System 3.0 and the Hybrid Hierarchical Predictive Control System. The 2.0L has 110 kW and 149 ps, or 148 hp. Last but not least, an “extensive suite” of SmartSense Advanced Driver Assistance Systems help the driver and enhance occupant protection more than before.

2027 McLaren MCL41 to Become the Second F1 Car to Be Sold Before It's Raced
6 photos
Photo: McLaren
At the end of last year, Formula 1 team McLaren Racing and auction house RM Sotheby’s did something no one had done before: they auctioned off one of the two MCL40 cars that were raced this season, before the cars were unveiled and campaigned in F1. The vehicle became the first Formula 1 car to be auctioned before being raced, and it went for an astonishing $11,480,000. And now they're doing it again.
With just three races left in the season, and the two titles, Drivers' Championship and Constructors' Championship, already claimed by Andrea Kimi Antonelli and Mercedes, respectively, the eyes of the world are already looking at the next season, which is set to kick off in March 2027.
With that in mind, McLaren and RM Sotheby’s teamed up once more for a redo of last year's stunt. The focus of the partnership is the sale of one of the two chassis to be used by the team next season, a piece of hardware that will be known as MCL41.
The car is yet to be unveiled, but it will, naturally, be built to adhere to the new rules of the competition, which include, among other things, an increase in engine power from 400 kW to 420 kW, a decrease in the power of the motor-generator unit-kinetic from 350 kW to 300 kW, and a five percent fuel flow increase, among other things.
We also know that the car will be powered by a Mercedes-AMG powerplant, and, naturally, that it will wear a new livery, better suited for the 2027 season.
Now, selling one of the two MCL41 chassis doesn't mean the car will actually end up in the buyer's possession immediately. McLaren will take the money, race the car in Formula 1 , and only at a later date, after the 2027 season is over, will it deliver the vehicle to its owner.
Depending on who drives the MCL41 and how the season ends, the buyer will either be left with a disappointing piece of hardware on their hands, or with something that could be worth a lot more than the money paid for it as the final checkered flag waves.
The 2027 will go under the hammer on December 9 at the Saadiyat Grove Experience Center in Abu Dhabi, right after the Formula 1 final race of the season at the Yas Marina Circuit. The MCL41 will not be on site, of course, but that will probably not keep people from bidding for it.
The winner of the auction will be given the option to choose what car they'll get, be it the one to be driven by 2025 World Champion Lando Norris , or by his partner, Oscar Piastri. Because, yes, the two men remain on deck with McLaren for next season.
The buyer will get not only the car, but also something the team describes as an unprecedented package of extras. That includes exclusive access to the McLaren Racing team to meet Zak Brown and the two drivers, an invitation to the official public launch, and free access to a number of races: the Monaco GP, 24 Hours of Le Mans, and Indianapolis 500 - these last two because McLaren Racing returns to the FIA World Endurance Championship as well next year.
Once the MCL41 is raced for the entirety of the season and is delivered to its new owner, it can be used in designated demonstration runs and at track days. If that happens, the British team also throws in official support with engineers and mechanics.

Burn It at the Stake! A Designer Set His Sights on a VW Transporter Van and Tried To Make It a Coupe
10 photos
Photo: Rowan Tuttle
Some vehicle designs simply change the game, and the VW Transporter isn’t one of the first to come to mind. However, there are some designers out there that have placed this vehicle in the spotlight and subjected it to the quirks of the depths of their mind.
The VW Transporter is clearly seen as a utilitarian vehicle, one that is used to carry the neighborhood kids to some soccer game, spotted at the heart of countless fleet operations across a wide range of industries, and even subjected to custom work , most often, in the form of a camper that people use to get away from it all. But, it is a workhorse machine, most-often spotted carrying your mail and Amazon packages to your door.
Photo: Volkswagen So, stumbling across a rendering project that explores vehicle design based around the Transporter is something that clearly sparked my interest. It’s called the Transporter Coupe and is the result of a question by its designer Rowan Tuttle: “SUV coupes are a thing. So why not a Transporter with a twist?” A question that very few, if anyone has ever thought of asking.
Maybe some Japanese craftsman or woman has thought of doing so, integrating this sort of look into their wild and transformative van culture. “Vanning” they call it, and some of the designs to come out from this subculture are simply insane. While I’ve never seen a “van coupe,” someone is bound to have thought of it.
Now, all we have to give us an idea of what this design is meant to bring to the table is one or two renderings mixed in with some AI-generated images, the latter standing as a shortcut to visualizing a design that is clearly difficult to image, not to mention putting aside purist design views in order to give rise to such a horrendous monstrosity.
Photo: Volkswagen I mean, I’m not the most car-inclined guy out there, but I do have a couple of favorite brands, with VW being one of them, so whenever is see an exploration around a vehicle they bring to the table, I like to check it out, and in seeing this Transporter Coupe, I can say that I was a bit disgusted; the exploration looks horrible, and it isn’t one that I would ever pay to own, so Tuttle seems to have answered his own question with the design.
I’m curious to read what you have to say about this deep-dive into a side of vehicle design that is rarely, if ever crossed. There’s a comment section below where you can do that.
As for myself, there are a few things I do want to point out, and one of the most obvious is that the ability to accommodate up to nine guests goes out the window, with the slanted and chopped rear of the van removing the necessary headroom for another row of guests. From what I can make out, only up to seven can now be accommodated in the van, maybe even less.
Photo: Rowan Tuttle Not only is the rear of the vehicle reduced, but judging by the size of the side doors, the chassis is also reduced in length. So, any idea that this “Transporter” is to be used in the same way that a real one would goes out the window.
Clearly, converting something like this into a camper van may still be on the menu, but again, it’s bound to be an experience that’s unlike what we’re used to, and the chopped rear is responsible for that once again.
Since space for a bed will be limited inside, so will the ability to integrate a kitchen, dining area, or any other space, so if the Coupe would even make it to market, it’s going to be a no-go for a camper conversion. At best, you’ll be able to toss a bed in there. Maybe these limitations in utility is why we don’t see such a vehicle on the road, or don’t we.
Photo: BMW I’ll be honest and without trying to hurt anyone’s feeling, I may have seen vehicles with a similar rear end before, and there are two that comes to mind. The first is the obvious Tesla Cybertruck, although, it is a bit of an exaggeration, and the second is the BMW X6. I’m going to receive some hate from X6 owners for that last one, but the resemblance is uncanny. Again, just the rear end.
What the concept would look like if it did have the traditional rear end would closely resemble a Scion XB, a discontinued vehicle and brand that some of us weren’t even around when it was “popular.” I won’t lie; I liked it, but I’ve always had a love for quirky cars and vehicles.
However, I can’t say that the Transporter Coupe is a vehicle I like, nor would I ever drop the bucks on one if it ever made it to market. I’m starting ti understand why this sort of look isn’t found in vehicles on the road today.

Ford Is Recalling F-150 Trucks in China for Improperly Secured Fuel Tank Straps
6 photos
Photo: Ford
Ford has determined that 54 exported trucks may have been produced with fuel tanks that may detach from the F-150 without warning. Assembled in the United States of America, said half-ton pickups were shipped to China, where American trucks carry a very different cultural meaning from their utilitarian roots.
Per a release from the Chinese State Administration for Market Regulation, the Ford Motor Company's local dealers will inspect F-150 vehicles produced for model years 2023 through 2025 from May 5, 2023, through October 16, 2024. Service technicians are to check both the front and rear fuel tank straps, where they attach to the frame's longitudinal beams.
If the straps appear to be iffy, dealers will replace them at no charge whatsoever to affected customers. Obviously enough, the potential consequences of an improperly secured fuel tank are pretty bad. The straps may loosen as the vehicle accumulates mileage, especially when it encounters the usual road imperfections.
When the straps loosen too much, fuel might escape the tank, resulting in an engine stall. Dropping from the vehicle while driving is another possibility, increasing the risk of a fire while creating a hazard for traffic behind the subject pickup. The Dearborn-based automaker has already dealt with this problem in the United States as part of recall 26V578.
Internally referred to as 26S69, the American campaign went live in September 2026. Similar to the Chinese recall, dealers were instructed to inspect the straps and replace them as they see fit. Both campaigns involve the very same F-150 generation, yet the Chinese recall is listed with fewer model years.
Photo: Ford China's F-150 issue further brings back memories of a single-vehicle recall from 2022, when a 2021 model was produced with the front fuel tank attachment bracket missing. At the time, Ford found no evidence that anyone at the plant had corrected the issue before giving the subject truck the green stamp of approval.
The current generation of the F-150 arrived in China in June 2022, first in the form of the Raptor off-road grade. Ford subsequently stopped sending US-built vehicles to China in April 2025, citing tariff escalation. China increased retaliatory tariffs at the time, with additional duties reaching a ginormous 125 percent.
China has since reduced the tariffs in question, and Ford's Chinese website continues promoting the F-150 Raptor. Care to guess how much this bad boy costs over there? 828,800 yuan is the listed starting price, converting to a staggering 124,350 dollars at current exchange rates. By comparison, the US-market Raptor is available from $75,325 (sans destination charge) at press time.
Back home in the United States, the F-150 underwent a few changes for model year 2027, starting with a new 3.0-liter EcoBoost twin-turbo V6 as the replacement for the previous 2.7-liter unit. The 5.0-liter Coyote naturally aspirated V8, meanwhile, returned as an option on the King Ranch and Platinum.
Hands-free driving while towing also needs highlighting, along with lower-priced equipment groups for the Tremor and Raptor. Last but not least, the first-ever Ford F-150 Carhartt made its debut as a $4,195 package on the 4x4 XLT SuperCrew.

Honda Avancier Debuts With Six Seats, New Logo, and New Hybrid Powertrain
13 photos
Photo: Honda
The all-new 2027 Honda Avancier arrives as a three-row, six-seat hybrid SUV. It comes with the next-generation hybrid powertrain and the newly styled brand logo, sits on a new platform, and is the first of 15 models of its kind that Honda plans to roll out globally by 2030.
Positioned above the CR-V in Honda’s lineup, the Avancier is the first hybrid model to wear Honda’s redesigned, minimalist "H" logo , which matches its entire design. The Avancier features sharp horizontal lines, smooth body surfaces, flush-fitting door handles, and a dramatically sloping roofline.
The model comes with a split-headlight front-end layout with slim upper LED daytime running lights and lower main beams, flanking a bold grille, paired with a full-width LED light bar and tall vertical accents, featuring straight lines and 90-degree angles out back, where a thin tailgate spoiler with a concealed rear wiper shows up.
Honda is obviously pushing for a visually uncluttered and sleek silhouette. Higher-spec models like the top-of-the-line RS ride on 20-inch alloy wheels and get blacked-out mirror caps and rear privacy glass for more drama.
Photo: Honda Unlike typical seven-seat models in the segment, the new Avancier launches strictly as a six-seater. The second row hosts two seats separated by a fold-down center console with cupholders for a limousine-like space and comfort.
Developed under the "Grand Journey" concept, the cabin can be specced with the optional Relaxation seats and upscale materials, along with a panoramic sunroof, which confirm its rivalry with the Hyundai Santa Fe, Kia Sorento, and Mazda CX-80.
Honda installed its 15-inch central touchscreen on board, along with a digital instrument cluster and an optional head-up display. The model sports a 12-speaker BOSE Premium Sound System, compatible with Dolby Atmos for an immersive 3D sound experience.
A voice recognition function for controlling features such as the air conditioning, Remote In-Cabin View, and Remote Surround View are also on the menu. Honda will add post-purchase features with over-the-air (OTA) updates.
Photo: Honda Honda keeps powertrain details under wraps, but the all-new Avancier, built on a newly developed lightweight architecture, replaces the previous e:HEV system with a new, downsized, higher-efficiency hybrid system.
The system is expected to integrate a 2.0-liter petrol engine with two electric motors, operating in the automaker’s first electric all-wheel-drive layout, the DualPower eAWD. The electric motors, one mounted out front and another driving the rear wheels, will work independently to put down power and improve off-the-line acceleration as well as stability.
The SUV is also equipped with the Motion Management System (MMS), an integrated vehicle-dynamics control technology that coordinates steering, braking force, and hybrid driving force to stabilize the SUV and sharpen its cornering.
The Avancier will also get the Honda S+ Shift, borrowed from the Prelude and Civic e:HEV RS, to simulate gear shifts and deliver a more engaging feel behind the wheel. The space was designed specifically to reduce physical strain and fatigue even during long-distance travel.
Photo: Honda The Honda Avancier will roll off the production line of the brand’s Prachinburi plant in Prachinburi Province, Thailand, and will launch first in Thailand, Japan and China before arriving in Australia and New Zealand in April 2027. The automaker currently has no plans to sell the Avancier in North America, where the larger Pilot and Passport fill the lineup.
Pricing has yet to be released, but Australian media claims the model is expected to start at around 60,000 Australian dollars, which translates to roughly $40,058 U.S. This would position it as a rival for the Hyundai Santa Fe, Kia Sorrento, and Toyota Highlander .
Honda has big hybrid plans The all-new Avancier is the first of 15 next-generation hybrid models that Honda will launch by the end of the fiscal year ending March 31, 2030. The plan follows a pivotal strategic moment when the automaker canceled almost its entire electric 0 lineup, including the 0 Saloon, 0 SUV , and Acura RSX, to reallocate funds to hybrids. Only the 0 Alpha has survived .
The Japanese automaker is expected to launch the next-generation Honda CR-V in 2027. Built on the same new midsize architecture as the all-new Avancier, the redesigned CR-V will arrive in North America as a hybrid-only crossover with the same 2.0-liter two-motor setup and DualPower eAWD.
In the meantime, the Civic and Accord, already previewed by the Honda Hybrid Sedan Prototype, are expected to debut around early 2028 and carry over the same hybrid system as the Avancier and the CR-V. The Acura Hybrid SUV Prototype previewed a future Acura RDX , set to arrive in either late 2027 or early 2028.
Honda has already announced a major wave of U.S. investments totaling more than $3.8 billion across its plants in Ohio, Alabama, and Georgia. The move follows the rising demand for hybrids and the tariffs imposed by the Trump administration on imported cars. The investments will help the Japanese automaker increase its production capacity to 1.3 million vehicles per year.

2026 LA Auto Show: Volkswagen Has Prepared a US-Only 2027 Golf GTI Rabbit Edition With Enhancements
11 photos
Photo: Volkswagen
Volkswagen joins the pool of automakers who dared to face the week of 'James Bondisson,' aka the casting of Robert Pattinson by Amazon MGM into the role of 007, Anthropic’s massive IPO, and especially the launch of GTA VI by attending the 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show.
Just before the start of the 2026 LA Auto Show, the preview for this year’s edition was looking bleak – we knew about the all-new Hyundai Elantra, the Rivian R2, and minor novelties and fresh limited editions from Kia, Acura, or Honda, and not much else.
Luckily, the carmakers decided to try and catch the spotlight a bit more, with the likes of the 2027 Chrysler Pacifica going Copperline. There was also the absolute best novelty, too – the 907-horsepower Lambo Temerario Spyder , which is a true work of Italian automotive art and technology, at least behind the seats, where an innovative retractable hardtop is stowed vertically to create a bespoke open-top experience that also improves handling via a lowered center of gravity.
Genesis also joined the party with the 2027 Genesis G80 and GV80 getting a brand-new hybrid powertrain featuring 347 hp and a first-ever liquid-cooled battery for a Hyundai Motor Group hybrid system. Volkswagen, which for the first time brought the all-new Atlas and Atlas Cross Sport family to Los Angeles, also decided to showcase the GTI Rabbit Edition at the Los Angeles Auto Show.
Volkswagen of America debuts a 2027.5 Volkswagen Golf GTI Rabbit special edition in California, a model that isn’t priced yet because the launch is only coming during the second quarter of next year. We do know that it’s tucked between the base S ($34,905) and the middle SE ($39,095) version, while the Autobahn ($42,595) remains at the top.
The 2027 Volkswagen Golf GTI Rabbit comes with both exterior and interior styling elements as well as “chassis upgrades designed to enhance cornering performance,” so it’s not all show with no extra go. The moniker is a tribute to the first VW Golf models offered in America starting in 1974, including the Rabbit GTI that was sold between 1982 and 1984, produced locally at Volkswagen’s Westmoreland, PA factory.
Now, the modern GTI Rabbit Edition comes with blacked-out design elements, a signature chrome Rabbit badge on the tailgate, as well as an exclusive color, Dark Moss Green Metallic, which is shared with Europe’s Golf GTI Edition 50 . Inside, there are race-inspired GTI Clubsport ArtVelours seat surfaces.
Additionally, the GTI Rabbit Edition has features from the GTI Autobahn and 19-inch wheels borrowed from the Golf R, plus the DCC adaptive damping system. The GTI Rabbit Edition is currently shown at the Los Angeles Auto Show until November 29, and after that it will be on display at the Motoring Coffee location in West LA from November 30 to December 4 and at the South OC Cars and Coffee on December 5.

Honda's 2027 Civic Range for the US Costs $300 More Across the Board, Welcomes Sport-L Grade
16 photos
Photo: Honda
American Honda Motor has given the 2027 Civic family a new member. The Sport-L, as implied by its name, is the fancier alternative to the Sport, and comes with heated front seats. Leather surfaces and power adjustments for the front seats are on the menu as well, along with dual-zone automatic climate control.
Priced at $28,495 for the sedan as opposed to $26,995 for the Sport grade, said newcomer is an interesting compact indeed. However, its MSRP will also make certain prospective customers think twice before pulling the trigger. The Sport Hybrid sedan is $29,695 before destination, and this $1,200 difference gets you a far more frugal powertrain that also happens to be punchier as well.
Beyond the aforementioned goodies, the Sport-L also includes blind-spot information with rear cross-traffic alert, silver gauge accents, the Honda Sensing driver-assistive and safety technologies, silver mesh trim for the instrument panel, a front passenger seatback pocket, and illuminated vanity mirrors. While not bad for the money, that Sport Hybrid grade also looks great on paper.
Those who view the Civic as nothing more than a relatively affordable means of personal transportation by 2027 model year standards are presented with the LX sedan, which is $24,995 from the outset. American Honda Motor lists a TSRP, namely a total suggested retail price, of $26,290 for the no-frills specification. Whichever you prefer, bear in mind that all 2027 Civic sedan and hatchback trims are $300 pricier than 2026 models at launch.
The priciest of the bunch are the Sport-L for the combustion-only Civic and the Sport Touring Hybrid for the less thirsty Civic. Up to 13 miles per gallon separate these powertrains, with American Honda Motor listing EPA-rated 36 miles per gallon (6.5 liters per 100 kilometers) for the LX sedan and 49 miles per gallon (4.8 liters per 100 kilometers) combined for the Sport Touring Hybrid sedan.
Photo: Honda Displacing 1,993 cubic centimeters, the base Atkinson-cycle naturally aspirated 2.0-liter engine of the LX, Sport, and Sport-L develops 150 horsepower and 133 pound-feet (180 Newton-meters). Exclusively front-wheel drive, just like the rest of the range, the 2.0-liter family uses a continuously variable transmission that improves efficiency to the detriment of driver enjoyment.
Also equipped with a 2.0-liter I4 of the free-breathing variety, the hybrids make 141 horsepower and 134 pound-feet (182 Newton-meters) without any hybrid assistance. Honda's two-motor hybrid system is rated at 181 ponies and 232 pound-feet (315 Newton-meters), yet combined system output is listed as 200 horsepower and more than sufficient peak torque for a compact.
Instead of a conventional CVT, a direct-drive arrangement with two electric motors is featured. An electronically controlled power unit and a lock-up clutch are listed as well. During suitable cruising conditions, said clutch connects the engine to the drive wheels. The hybrid further adds deceleration selectors for adjusting the intensity of the regenerative braking system.
Announced at the beginning of October 2026, the 2027 model year Civic Type R is the most powerful and thirstiest of the lot. Its 315-horse turbo inline-four and short-throw manual box carry over unchanged, yet Honda worked its magic in terms of auto rev matching, brake pedal feel, and suspension damping.
The CTR also received a retro engine cover inspired by earlier Japanese-market Type R models, along with a slightly different front fascia that includes a larger grille opening for improved cooling. Instead of $300, the Civic Type R jumped $1,300 from the 2026 model. Considering that American Honda Motor eliminated all no-cost paint colors for 2027, the effective jump is $1,755.

The Royal Australian Navy replenishment ship HMAS Stalwart's embarked MH-60R helicopter shown during a regional presence deployment. (Photo: Australian Department of Defence)
MELBOURNE – Australia has received the first two of 13 additional Sikorsky MH-60R Seahawk naval helicopters, expanding the Royal Australian Navy’s maritime aviation fleet.
The helicopters were delivered to the Royal Australian Navy (RAN) base HMAS Albatross near Nowra in New South Wales, Au stralia’s Department of Defence announced Thursday.
The delivery marks the first pair of 13 helicopters purchased from Lockheed Martin subsidiary Sikorsky Australia in 2022 under Canberra’s Project SEA9100 Phase 1, which aims to expand the RAN’s helicopter fleet. The acquisition included 12 additional MH-60Rs and a 13th aircraft to replace one lost during operations in 2021.
The helicopters will increase the RAN’s Seahawk fleet fleet from 23 to 36 aircraft, with the remaining 11 helicopters are expected to arrive by early 2028, according to Sikorsky Australia.
The MH-60R is primarily designed for anti-submarine and anti-surface warfare, but can also conduct intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance; maritime strike; search and rescue; and logistics support missions. The helicopters are equipped with a sensor suite, as well as Mark 54 lightweight torpedoes and Hellfire air-to-surface missiles.
Increasing the Royal Australian Navy’s Seahawk fleet “will allow the ADF to effectively operate in complex maritime environments and enhance its ability to defend Australia’s maritime approaches and contribute to regional security across the Indo-Pacific,” the Australian Defence Department said in a statement.
Cliff Kyle, sustainment director at Lockheed Martin Australia, said the RAN’s expanded Seahawk fleet will extend the helicopter’s “proven capability across more Navy assets and operational environments, further strengthening Australia’s ability to detect and respond to surface and subsurface threats.”
The first two helicopters completed flight testing in the United States before being transported to Australia, according to Lockheed Martin. The aircraft will undergo RAN-specific modifications before entering service, which is expected in April 2027, Deputy Prime Minister and Defense Minister Richard Marles said in a statement.
Australia initially sought 12 additional MH-60Rs for its fleet, with the $503 million Foreign Military Sales contract for the helicopters awarded by Naval Air Systems Command in August 2022.
However, the 13th helicopter was subsequently added to the contract to replace an MH-60R lost while attempting to land on board the destroyer HMAS Brisbane in the Philippine Sea in October 2021.

GTA 6 Review: The Beautiful Depraved Life
128 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution
Zlatan and Totti were still playing, and man, watching them on the pitch was amazing. Barack Obama was President. The Wolf of Wall Street came out. Apple took the wraps off the iPhone 5s, and Android was only at version 4.4.
Feeling old yet? You should. Because that’s how much has passed since the debut of GTA 5 .
The world has never waited so long for a video game, and more importantly, the world has never waited so long for a video game without losing its interest. GTA 6 is undoubtedly the biggest game release in history, and despite the super-bumpy road between 2013 and November 19, 2026, it’s still the topic on everybody’s lips.
I won’t insist much on what happened before the launch because we’ve all been following the news. A leak caused a painful delay, and so many people claimed the GTA franchise was done. Nobody could afford such a big delay, and 13 years between releases would be the final nail in its coffin. None of these happened, and GTA 6 is still a phenomenon.
I remember that a few years ago, a source who claimed they were familiar with Rockstar’s GTA 6 efforts posted on Twitter (yes, it was still called Twitter, that’s how old you are) that the company wanted to make this game the biggest release in history. Employees were working late, sometimes until 3 AM, just to get GTA 6 right.
It doesn’t even matter if this alleged leak was accurate or just wishful thinking. Rockstar did manage to make GTA 6 the biggest release in history.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution With Trevor (oh, I miss Trevor), Michael, and Franklin gone, GTA 6 is now based on the story of Jason and Lucia. That’s how the game starts , and if you haven’t played GTA 6 before - though there’s a good chance that you, at least, watched some videos because the whole world is talking about it - you’d better grab a large bag of popcorn for the two chapters.
The introductory chapters are supposed to let you get to know Jason and Lucia. They meet when Jason’s trying to steal the car Lucia stole “for her mother,” with the cops showing up exactly when the two were fighting. They are about to get arrested when Lucia tells the police they were a couple arguing about who to drive.
Seconds later, they beat the cops and run away. Long story short, the two fall in love, have a baby, and Lucia ends up in prison. You start the game with Jason, who has simple missions to do at first, such as running some errands for Brian and recovering a car impounded by the police.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Just to be clear, while GTA 6 feels a lot like GTA, it’s not exactly GTA. I know this doesn’t make much sense at first - and that wouldn’t be a surprise, I’m typing these words after playing GTA 6 for 6 hours - but Rockstar wanted the original concept of Grand Theft Auto to evolve significantly with this release.
Jason and Lucia are no longer just pickpockets. That’s why you don’t have websites in the game . You don’t rob liquor stores, as Rockstar explains, and then spend all your money on a shopping site. Jason and Lucia are here for big heists, so you start small and advance in the game to more complex and sophisticated hits.
It’s still GTA because you can still drive around, enjoy the music, run a red light, fight an NPC, and so on. You can play the game however you like, and despite GTA 6 having just a single-player campaign - with no online mode currently available - the open world allows you to do pretty much anything you want.
Rockstar has eliminated the concept of replayability with Grand Theft Auto. Sure, you can still play the story from one end to another after you complete it once, but the magic of GTA is that you can do so many other things in the game that the campaign sometimes becomes the backup plan. When I was much younger - like 13 years ago - I enjoyed driving around the city, listening to the music, and waiting for the green light. Basically, I liked being a good citizen.
It’s harder not to be a good citizen in GTA 6. You now have a criminal profile, so the more you play, and obviously, the more illegal things you do, the more criminal activity you have on your record. Things like changing your outfit, the car color, and everything else are essential now because the police will continue to search for you even after you escape the cops.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution This is one of the best things about GTA 6. The criminal profile stays there, it doesn’t get erased when you walk away, so you could end up with a dozen cars chasing you for a minor thing like stealing a car. That’s because you previously hit a policeman and blew up 30 cars on the road.
Stealing cars is also more difficult than in GTA 5. The reason is simple. They are all locked and fitted with an alarm system, so when you steal a car, the alarm goes off. NPCs around you call the cops, describe how you look, and there you go- you’re getting another thing on your criminal record. Staying under the radar, such as driving the same car most of the time until you get the money to buy a better one, and avoiding stealing vehicles parked on the side of the road should always be on your agenda.
If you don’t want to steal a car, you can ride the bus. That’s right, you can now be part of the daily commute, so you can go to a bus station, wait for the bus to arrive, hop in, and go wherever you need to go. This is just another way to play GTA, so if you don’t feel like doing missions for Brian, you can always wake up early and be part of the working class, traveling by bus and so on.
Jason is a former paid security guard for people who don’t speak English, as he tells Cal, so he’s up to the task for whatever mission Brian throws at him. However, he gets better, and you’ll want to do little things like swimming, drinking water, and so on to improve certain stats.
It’s not just stealing cars and hitting pedestrians anymore.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution And speaking of pedestrians, NPCs are one of the most evolved parts of GTA 6. I remember hearing someone from Rockstar claiming that every NPC is unique, not necessarily by look but by the way it’s dressed. And that’s true.
Depending on which part of Leonida you are, NPCs look different. If you’re in the corporate zone, expect to see a lot of suits. If you’re in the industrial area, you’ll see different clothes, and so on. They also behave differently, so for example, truck drivers will gladly get outside of their vehicles to engage in combat if you somehow do something they don’t like, such as hitting their truck.
NPCs feel more alive than ever, and considering you play in a city, and a city is typically full of people, this is undoubtedly a fantastic upgrade.
You can rob people, but depending on who you rob, you’ll get beer money or a ton of money. I once robbed a construction worker and only took $3 and his cigarettes, but on the other hand, I followed a Grotti Furia driver (which is actually based on the Ferrari SF90 Stradale) and made over $100 in less than 10 seconds with just a punch.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Driving. Well, driving is a completely different story than what you’re familiar with from GTA 5. First of all, I think everybody knows by now that we’re getting an impressive collection of cars in GTA 6 - there are more than 600 - many of which use different names for obvious reasons.
The first car that you drive in GTA 6 is Jason’s 1970 Vapid Ganado, and considering that stealing cars is now a risky thing to do because the police will immediately be on your tail, you should do as many errands as possible behind its wheel.
The Ganado is a 1970 Ford Ranchero , the car that Ford originally launched in the late ‘50s and which competed against Chevrolet’s El Camino (before GM gave up on the fight and retired the El Camino in 1960, eventually to relaunch it later in the same decade).
There are absolutely no doubts that you’ll be tempted to steal other cars. You’ll come across super beautiful machines, including the Progen Emerus (which is actually a McLaren Senna ) and the Inventero Coquette D10 (a fictional name for the Corvette C8).
If your criminal record goes through the roof, you’ll end up being chased by the Pegassi Tempesta, which is just Rockstar’s way of calling the Lamborghini Huracan.
But the actual driving, no matter what car you choose, is more challenging now. The reason comes down to the new mechanics, which make the game less chaotic. You’re not supposed to ram into anything and everything anymore. Hitting a larger vehicle will significantly damage yours, and repeatedly crashing into cars will cause problems that will prevent you from finishing your mission.
You can also run out of gas, so if you steal a car to run away from the cops, don’t be too surprised if you jump behind the wheel of an Audi with an empty tank - been there, done that, so much swearing from both me and Jason.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Jason is always carrying a phone, so when you drive and he looks at the screen, you’ll have half of what you see blocked. Hats off to Rockstar for doing this because, in some ways, this idea also helps educate drivers that driving and using a mobile phone don’t work together .
Jason does it, but it’s not as easy as you think to rush to complete a mission and not hit something on the road because you look at the screen.
The car mechanics are more accurate than ever, and despite not getting anywhere close to racing games such as Gran Turismo, this isn’t even supposed to happen. It’s still GTA, but the evolved concept allows you to feel like you’re actually driving a car. There’s a lot of feedback, at least on PlayStation 5, so you’ll have the controller vibrate all the time, just to make you feel as if you were there in Jason’s seat.
Driving at night is a completely different story. This is what I consider to be the most difficult part of the game, especially when you’re against the clock and with the police on your tail. I figured this out from the first missions when you’re supposed to recover the Phoenix from the police impound.
Figuring out which way to go with so many police cars ramming you is quite challenging, and I can only imagine that it gets a lot more difficult as you advance in the game. The amount of glare from the other headlights, and everything shining around you when it’s raining, make some missions a lot harder than they’d be during daytime.
I found that adjusting the graphics settings in the game and on my TV, especially the HDR settings, helped, but there’s a lot of trial and error to get everything right. For example, I also configured the camera to the highest level to be able to see above my car and observe more of the incoming traffic.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution The graphics and level of detail are impressive, top-notch, exquisite- you name it. There’s a lot of talk online about Rockstar’s decision to limit GTA 6 to 30 fps . Sure, this isn’t necessarily the best setting, but Rockstar said that the complex world in GTA 6 would make handling all the resources a massive challenge even for the PS5 Pro.
There’s an obvious improvement if you play the game on a standard non-Pro PS5 and then switch to a PS5 Pro, but Rockstar claims the Pro wouldn’t be able to handle 60 fps.
However, I think Rockstar got it right. It’s 30 fps, but considering GTA 6 is custom-built - everything is custom-built, according to the company - the game reached a perfect balance that doesn’t make it feel like you’re playing in 30 fps. I heard some people are experiencing a drop in fps when playing on the Xbox Series S, but no such thing is happening on the standard PS5.
Otherwise, my God, this is a beautiful game. I spend maybe an hour admiring the beautiful Leonida, the buildings, the gardens, the ocean, the cars, everything. Rockstar has put a lot of effort into getting every little detail right, including even the hair on Jason’s legs.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution While driving feels more challenging at first, flying a plane is a lot easier, for some reason. That’s how you start the game, as you need to land a plane on water and tell Brian that you failed. Doing this without any prior attempts is so easy, and it remains easy throughout the game.
GTA 6 continues to introduce you to so many types of vehicles, and you can even rent a scooter because it’s 2026, and we have electric scooters getting in our way pretty much all over the city.
The weapon system has been majestically improved, and I must applaud Rockstar for the level of detail that every single gun offers in GTA 6. Aiming isn’t necessarily as straightforward and convenient as you’d expect it to be, though, and there’s a major learning curve here.
I played the game with the default settings, and aiming right was, let’s say, difficult enough to make me use the same language as some of the NPCs in GTA 6. I once even gave up on shooting my enemies and used my fists to get rid of them, just because it was easier this way. Sure, you’ll still have to improve your aiming, and I recommend that you use the stores around you for as much training as possible.
You won’t want to fire your weapon outside like a mad man because the cops will be there in a second, and as I already told you, that’s not by any means a good thing.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution THE BOTTOM LINE To be honest, I feel like I could go on forever to tell you how great and captivating GTA 6 can be, and this only says a lot about the work Rockstar has put into this game in the last 13 years.
The wait was certainly worth it, but more importantly, it was absolutely necessary for a company, even the size of Rockstar, to bring the Grand Theft Auto franchise to the point where it is today.
In some ways, I think the leak that caused the frustrating delay a few years ago was beneficial to the franchise. Rockstar got more time to get everything right, and playing GTA 6 confirms that the company managed to do this in a remarkable way. Waiting that long for GTA 6 wasn’t easy, and I can only imagine the pressure Rockstar and its staff have been trying to deal with in the last few years when everybody lost their patience.
It’s hard to find something to hate about GTA 6. This isn’t an exaggeration, and while some things can be improved, such as the night driving, everything comes with a learning curve that, once you master it, makes a lot more sense. The same for aiming, which isn’t necessarily easy at first, but the more you play, the easier it gets (or the better you get, obviously).
GTA 6 is undoubtedly the game of the year, but beyond that, it’s the game of the decade. There’s one little thing that many people seem to ignore.
With the release of GTA 6, Rockstar has pushed the gaming world to a completely new level. It raised the bar of what we’re getting from new-generation games, and not matching this level will create utter disappointment for each and every one of us. That’s a problem even for Rockstar, as the next Grand Theft Auto, whenever it’ll land, must be a masterpiece.
For Rockstar’s rivals, this thing is even “more” impossible. It’s not like Grand Theft Auto has ever had a competitor, but if Trevor, Franklin, and Michael continued to be relevant even after 13 years - because yes, some people are still playing GTA 5 - I can only imagine that Jason and Lucia will dominate the gaming world for quite some time. Time will tell how GTA 6 will age, but Rockstar has the know-how to milk every dollar from its games, so it’s safe to assume that more updates and goodies will be released in the coming years. Including a PC version.
In its current form, GTA 6 is a game that sooner or later everybody will play. The only shortcoming right now is that it’s exclusive to consoles, so an important part of the gaming community - the ones on PC - are left behind for the time being. There are options to deal with this, and I’ve heard that some people are renting their PlayStations when they’re not playing GTA 6 to let others play the game from their PCs via Remote Play.
That’s how big GTA has become. People are renting their consoles, others are taking time off from work just to play the game. Heck, even my 68-year-old mother heard of GTA and asked me to send her a gameplay video to see what it’s all about. It’s not just a game anymore, it’s a phenomenon that’ll remain in history forever.
Rockstar’s accomplishment is even more impressive when you inspect GTA 6 down to its smallest detail. It’s a mix of so many bad things happening in our lives, including guns, drugs, alcohol, and the power money can give to any individual. All of these are mixed with a satirical approach and turned into a recipe that we can all digest with so much excitement.
GTA 6 is just a beautiful, depraved life.
